subject: science
passage: On the morning of June 30, 1908, an enormous explosion shook a remote forest near the Podkamennaya Tunguska River in Siberia. Because the region was so isolated, no scientific team reached it until 1927, when an expedition led by the mineralogist Leonid Kulik finally arrived. Kulik found no crater. Instead, millions of trees, stripped of their branches and pointing away from a central area, ______ flattened across more than 2,000 square kilometers, evidence that most researchers now attribute to a comet or asteroid that burst apart in the air before reaching the ground.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The sentence needs a main verb for the subject "millions of trees," and the meaning is that the trees were resting on the ground, which is the verb "lie." The past tense of "lie" is "lay," which fits the past-tense narrative ("found," "arrived"). "Laid" is the past tense of "lay," a different verb that means to put something down and needs an object.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Laying" is a participle of "lay" (to put something down), so the sentence would have no main verb.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Laid" is the past tense of "lay," which means to put something down and requires an object; the trees were not putting anything down.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Lain" is the past participle of "lie" and cannot be the main verb without a helping verb such as "had."
explanation.D: Correct. "Lay," the past tense of "lie," gives the subject a main verb and correctly says the trees were resting on the ground.
